items.title: 1. Receive the Task
items.body: The task may arrive on paper or electronically. Wait until the judge and participants are ready before beginning.

items.title: 2. Read and Analyze the Task
items.body: Read the task silently. The group usually asks someone to read it once aloud. Use this time to identify WHO, WHAT, HOW, WHERE, and useful SEARCH TERMS.

items.title: 3. Clarify the Task
items.body: Discuss what the task means. Reach a shared understanding of what the group must accomplish.

items.title: 4. Establish Direction
items.body: After clarification, develop an agenda or propose a consensus question based on the task.

items.title: 5. Research
items.body: Students typically spend approximately five minutes locating useful evidence in their research materials.

items.title: 6. Transition into Background and Discussion
items.body: Share essential background and move into substantive discussion. Re-clarify only if an important uncertainty remains.
